authoritative_precedence_note: The HGL preface states that Part XLV and Appendices BO–BW supersede conflicting earlier boundary-identity, category-map, axis, coordinate-successor, dimensional-limit, limit-machine, quality-at-limit, proof, worked-example and compiler statements; Part XLIV and Part XLIII retain their stated narrower authorities. Explanations in this batch therefore describe each owned part faithfully while flagging later-authority risk instead of silently treating earlier formulations as final where conflict is possible.

coverage.note: Initial source-addressed batch; continuing through major parts 31–48.

parts.title: Part XXII — Anti-collapse rules
parts.explanation: A concentrated error-prevention layer. It forbids collapsing FemaleType/MaleType into standalone PA routes; reversing IH projection; moving NOT through IH or PA; distributing IH automatically; flattening nested inheritance; erasing source indices; replacing full HGL identity with Boolean projection; resurrecting superseded Stage-2 forms; equating opposite-side non-states with the next stage; reading higher stage as >100% female/male; or inferring exact anatomy, maturity, psychology, social role or guaranteed traits without bridge laws. The rules operationalize the source’s typed/provenance-preservation discipline.
reader_cautions: The list spans a page boundary before the next major heading; use the TOC heading boundary, not a simplistic page-only split, when auditing individual numbered rules.
Later hyperordinal/boundary claims are subject to the preface’s explicit later-authority precedence.

parts.title: Part XXIII — Glossary
parts.explanation: Defines the working vocabulary needed to keep category, cause, provenance, phenotype and temporal development separate. It characterizes Archfemale/Archmale and the wider Archwomanhood/Archmanhood hierarchy; FemaleType/MaleType; PA and PA irreducibility; inner/outer negation; IH, projection and provenance; inheritance depth and Boolean projection; the antithetically productive zig-zag; interstage versus intrastage development; deduction/inference labels; and the phenotype map. Its main reader value is term-disambiguation rather than adding a new proof rule.
reader_cautions: Glossary hierarchy/boundary wording must be read under the source’s later-authority precedence if Part XLV or BO–BW conflicts with it.

parts.title: Part XXIV — Remaining open questions after the IH revision
parts.explanation: Separates unresolved variables from already-closed defects. Open issues include when logically equivalent formulas count as the same IH source, which source properties are inheritable, whether any special IH distribution law may later exist, whether stage regression or skipping is physically allowed, transition continuity, the exact phenotype map, phenotype retention, phenotype convergence/divergence across genealogies and environments, and causal realization of hyperordinal/limit transitions. The conservative defaults preserve HGL-defining properties and provenance without inventing transition laws.
reader_cautions: Open questions are not permission to fill gaps by intuition; absent transition/phenotype laws remain explicitly unspecified.
Some open-question text continues before the next major heading on the following page even though the TOC start-page metadata advances there.

parts.title: Part XXV — Inference matrix for common statements
parts.explanation: A compact claim-status matrix that labels common formulas as core distinctions, axioms, deductions, theorems, rejections or causal inferences. It reinforces PA negation-scope and irreducibility, one-way IH projection, IH-negation scope, nonflattening of nested inheritance, predecessor entailment through stage recursion, rejection of SF1⇒PA(x), separation of stage from visible trait and development, and the requirement for explicit causal laws before phenotype deduction. It is an epistemic lookup table for preventing overclaiming.
reader_cautions: The matrix states status under the then-current formal core; later-authoritative revisions control if a boundary/hyperordinal statement conflicts.

parts.title: Part XXVI — Compact canonical formal specification
parts.explanation: Implementation-facing snapshot of the PH-enhanced core. It types PA, IH and PH; states primitive PA modes and anti-distribution rules; preserves IH projection/provenance and PH irreducibility; fixes SF1/SM1; gives the eight-conjunct SF2/SM2 base; defines local successor recursion, FemaleType/MaleType, inheritance depth, phenotype-source order and occupancy-based Archfemale/Archmale labels; and explicitly separates zero Archstage change from zero woman/man development. It is a high-density reference, not a license to discard the fuller source context.
reader_cautions: The source preface gives later parts explicit precedence over conflicting boundary identities, category maps, hyperordinal/limit rules and compiler rules; use this part as the compact local core, not automatically the final authority on later-revised boundary mechanics.

parts.title: Part XXVII — Temporal and developmental logic of Archfemales and Archmales
parts.explanation: A major temporal-developmental formalization. It separates Hypergendered stage S(a,t), sex-related maturity/development D(a,t), and complete biological realization B(a,t); distinguishes interstage progression from intrastage development; represents each stage as a fiber/family of possible biological realizations; proves that temporary or permanent stage stagnation does not entail developmental or phenotypic stasis; treats puberty as one intrastage process rather than a synonym for Archstage progression; separates stage acquisition, expression and maturation; distinguishes stage velocity from stage identity; and supports occupancy-based Archfemale/Archmale classification even at zero stage velocity. The part’s central crosspattern is nonidentity among stage, maturity and full phenotype despite causal interaction among them.
reader_cautions: Do not infer a frozen body from constant Archstage, or Archstage advancement from puberty alone.

Long-form temporal claims should be checked against later-authoritative revisions where boundary/limit mechanics are implicated, while the stage-versus-development distinction remains source-explicit here.
